title: Cassini and d'Ocagne for the Full Horadam Recurrence — the Geometric Constant (−q)ⁿ
description: The parent entry (fibonacci-identities-oq-04-oq-01) proved Vajda's product identities for every solution of the *Fibonacci* recurrence G(n+2)=G(n+1)+G(n), replacing the Cassini sign (−1)ⁿ by the discriminant μ=a²−ab−b². Its second open question asks to push the constant to the full Horadam recurrence H(n+2)=p·H(n+1)+q·H(n) with arbitrary p,q∈ℤ, where the controlling constant is no longer a fixed sign but the geometric factor (−q)ⁿ. This entry supplies that generalization. Fix parameters p,q and seeds H(0)=a, H(1)=b. The headline result is the two-index d'Ocagne identity for Horadam sequences H(n+k+1)·H(n) − H(n+k)·H(n+1) = (−q)ⁿ·(H(k+1)·a − H(k)·b), proved by a single induction on n that applies the recurrence twice in the step. Cassini/Simson is the k=1 case H(n+2)·H(n) − H(n+1)² = (−q)ⁿ·(H(2)·a − b²), whose constant H(2)·a − b² = (p·b+q·a)·a − b² is the Horadam discriminant. For the Fibonacci numbers (p,q,a,b)=(1,1,0,1) the discriminant is −1 and (−q)ⁿ=(−1)ⁿ, recovering the textbook Cassini identity in the shifted form F(n+2)·F(n) − F(n+1)² = (−1)ⁿ⁺¹. The geometric factor (−q)ⁿ is exactly det(M)ⁿ for the companion matrix M=[[p,q],[1,0]] (det M=−q), the Horadam analogue of the Q=[[1,1],[1,0]] viewpoint of the parent hierarchy. Fully verified: 0 sorries, 0 axioms, no native_decide.

overview.historicalContext: Cassini's identity (G. D. Cassini, 1680; rediscovered by R. Simson, 1753) F(n+1)F(n−1) − F(n)² = (−1)ⁿ and d'Ocagne's identity are the foundational product relations of the Fibonacci numbers. The same product structure holds for any second-order linear recurrence: A. F. Horadam (1965) studied the two-parameter family W(n+2) = pW(n+1) + qW(n) — the Horadam sequences — which subsumes Fibonacci, Lucas, Pell, Jacobsthal and the Mersenne-like sequences. For such a recurrence the companion matrix is M = [[p, q],[1, 0]] with determinant −q, so the multiplicative constant in every Cassini-type identity is (−q)ⁿ rather than a fixed sign. The parent Vajda entry proved the product hierarchy for the p=q=1 family (general seeds, discriminant μ = a²−ab−b²); this entry answers its second open question by carrying the identities to arbitrary p, q.
overview.problemStatement:
**Open Question (fibonacci-identities-oq-04-oq-01, #2)**: Extend the product identities to the full Horadam recurrence W(n+2) = pW(n+1) + qW(n) with p, q ≠ 1, where the controlling constant becomes a function of p, q and the seeds.

**Result**: horadam_dOcagne — for the Horadam sequence H with H(0)=a, H(1)=b, H(n+2)=p·H(n+1)+q·H(n), the two-index identity H(n+k+1)·H(n) − H(n+k)·H(n+1) = (−q)ⁿ·(H(k+1)·a − H(k)·b) holds for all k, n; its k=1 case is the generalized Cassini identity horadam_cassini, and the classical Fibonacci Cassini fib_cassini_shifted follows by specialization.
overview.text: A Horadam sequence is any solution of H(n+2) = p·H(n+1) + q·H(n), parametrised by the two parameters (p,q) and the two seeds (a,b) = (H(0), H(1)). For each fixed gap k the quantity D_k(n) = H(n+k+1)·H(n) − H(n+k)·H(n+1) satisfies D_k(n+1) = −q·D_k(n), so D_k(n) = (−q)ⁿ·D_k(0); the gap-1 case is Cassini. The constant (−q)ⁿ is the n-th power of det[[p,q],[1,0]] = −q, exposing the matrix mechanism behind the identity.
overview.proofStrategy:
**Proof Strategy.**

1. **Define the sequence.** H p q a b : ℕ → ℤ by structural recursion: H 0 = a, H 1 = b, H (n+2) = p·H(n+1) + q·H n. The recurrence lemma H_rec is then definitional (rfl).
2. **The master induction.** Prove horadam_dOcagne by induction on n with k fixed. The base n=0 is the definition of the constant (both sides equal H(k+1)·a − H(k)·b). For the step, normalize the shifted indices (n+1+k+1 = (n+k)+2, etc. via omega), expand H((n+k)+2) and H(n+2) with H_rec, and close with linear_combination (−q)·(induction hypothesis): the two recurrence expansions make the new difference exactly −q times the old one.
3. **Cassini as k=1.** horadam_cassini specializes horadam_dOcagne at k=1 and rewrites H(n+1)·H(n+1) as the square; horadam_cassini_const evaluates H 2 = p·b + q·a from the recurrence.
4. **Recover Fibonacci.** H_fib shows H 1 1 0 1 = Nat.fib by strong induction (the two-step recurrence matches Nat.fib_add_two). Substituting into horadam_cassini and evaluating the discriminant fib(2)·0 − 1² = −1 with (−q)ⁿ = (−1)ⁿ gives the classical Cassini identity in shifted form, F(n+2)·F(n) − F(n+1)² = (−1)ⁿ⁺¹.
keyInsights: **The constant is geometric, not a sign.** For the general recurrence the Cassini multiplier is (−q)ⁿ = det[[p,q],[1,0]]ⁿ. The Fibonacci sign (−1)ⁿ is just the q=1 case; the determinant of the companion matrix is the single object that controls the whole product hierarchy.

**One induction proves two classical identities at once.** Keeping the gap k a free parameter turns Cassini (k=1) and d'Ocagne (general k) into a single statement D_k(n) = (−q)ⁿ·D_k(0). No separate induction is needed for either; d'Ocagne and Cassini are the same theorem read at different gaps.

**The step is a clean telescoping.** Expanding both H(n+k+2) and H(n+2) by the recurrence cancels the p-terms and leaves D_k(n+1) = −q·D_k(n) exactly — the inductive step is therefore a one-line linear_combination over ℤ, with no parity or case analysis.

**Specialization is free.** Because H is defined for arbitrary integer parameters, the classical Fibonacci Cassini, and every other named recurrence (Lucas q=1, Pell p=2 q=1, Jacobsthal p=1 q=2), are instances obtained by fixing (p,q,a,b) — no re-proof required.

conclusion.summary: Complete, fully verified (0 sorries, 0 axioms, no native_decide) generalization of the Cassini/Simson and d'Ocagne identities from the Fibonacci recurrence to the full two-parameter Horadam recurrence H(n+2)=p·H(n+1)+q·H(n). The master result horadam_dOcagne — H(n+k+1)·H(n) − H(n+k)·H(n+1) = (−q)ⁿ·(H(k+1)·a − H(k)·b) — has Cassini as its k=1 case and is proved by a single induction on n; the classical Fibonacci Cassini identity is recovered as a corollary.
conclusion.implications: Answers open question #2 of the parent Vajda/Gibonacci entry, showing that the product-identity hierarchy lifts from the unit recurrence (p=q=1) to every second-order integer linear recurrence, with the companion-matrix determinant −q as the single controlling constant. The Lucas (q=1), Pell (p=2,q=1) and Jacobsthal (p=1,q=2) Cassini identities are now instances obtained by fixing the four parameters.
openQuestions: Prove the full two-index Vajda / Catalan identity for Horadam sequences, H(n+i)·H(n+j) − H(n)·H(n+i+j) = (−q)ⁿ·(closed form in i, j and the seeds), generalizing the parent's μ·Fᵢ·Fⱼ to arbitrary p, q.
Formalize the companion-matrix proof directly: show Mⁿ = [[H'-style entries]] for M = [[p,q],[1,0]] and deduce the Cassini constant (−q)ⁿ from det(Mⁿ) = (det M)ⁿ via Matrix.det_pow.
Establish the Gibonacci/Horadam analogue of the Gelin–Cesàro identity, pairing the k=1 and k=3 d'Ocagne instances as a difference of squares.

crossReferences.description: Resolves open question #2 of the parent (extend the discriminant constant to the full Horadam recurrence with p, q ≠ 1), carrying the Cassini/d'Ocagne identities from the p=q=1 Gibonacci family to arbitrary linear recurrences with constant (−q)ⁿ.

The grandparent Vajda entry proved the product hierarchy over the Fibonacci numbers; this entry generalizes the Cassini and d'Ocagne members of that hierarchy to every second-order integer linear recurrence.
